question: To which patient group do standard precautionary measures apply?

options.A: All patients receiving care regardless of diagnosis
options.B: Only patients with confirmed infectious diseases
options.C: Individuals showing visible symptoms of bleeding
options.D: Patients admitted to surgical wards exclusively

explanation: Standard precautions are universal infection control practices intended for every patient encounter, irrespective of their infection status. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h1)

question: Which bodily fluid is excluded from the application of standard precautions?
explanation: Sweat is non-infectious regarding bloodborne and standard transmission routes, so it is excluded from standard precaution fluids. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h1)

question: What is the recommended duration for routine hand hygiene using an alcohol-based rub?
explanation: Alcohol-based hand rubbing requires 20 to 30 seconds of friction to effectively reduce microbial load on non-soiled hands. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h2)

question: When is soap and water handwashing strictly preferred over alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids
options.D: When exiting a patient room without touching surfaces

explanation: Physical dirt and organic material physically shield microorganisms, requiring mechanical removal with soap and water. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of wearing a medical gown during specific clinical procedures?

options.A: To maintain a sterile surgical field for the patient
options.B: To replace the need for hand hygiene after patient contact
options.C: To keep the healthcare worker warm in cold clinical areas
options.D: To prevent soiling of clothing and protect skin from splashes

explanation: Gowns create a barrier to protect the worker's uniform and skin from contact with infectious body fluids. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h3)

question: What action should be taken immediately after removing gloves and other personal protective equipment?

options.A: Document the procedure in the chart
options.D: Put on a fresh pair of gloves

explanation: Microorganisms can transfer to hands during the removal of PPE, making immediate hand hygiene mandatory. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h3)

question: At what capacity level must a sharps disposal container be closed and replaced?
explanation: Sharps containers should never be overfilled past the three-quarters mark to prevent accidental needle-sticks during disposal. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h4)

question: Why is two-handed needle recapping strictly discouraged in clinical practice?

options.A: It significantly increases the risk of accidental needle-stick injury
options.B: It wastes valuable nursing time during busy shifts
options.C: It violates medication dosage calculation standards
options.D: It damages the sharp tip, making future injections painful

explanation: Holding the cap with one hand while guiding a needle with the other frequently leads to accidental punctures of the guiding hand. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h4)

question: Where should a person direct their cough if a disposable tissue is not available?

options.A: Into the air away from people
options.B: Into the inner aspect of the elbow
options.D: Directly into the open palms of both hands

explanation: Coughing into the elbow prevents respiratory droplets from contaminating the hands, which frequently touch environmental surfaces. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h5)

question: A patient arrives at the outpatient clinic with a persistent cough and fever. What immediate intervention should be initiated at the entrance?

options.A: Administer broad-spectrum antibiotics to prevent transmission
options.B: Draw baseline blood cultures before allowing them to sit down
options.C: Isolate the patient in a private room for intravenous fluid resuscitation
options.D: Provide a surgical mask, tissues, and direct them to hand hygiene stations

explanation: Source control at the point of entry stops respiratory droplets from spreading in crowded waiting areas. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h5)

question: Which of the following represents a high-touch surface requiring frequent disinfection in a patient room?

options.B: Bed side rails and call buttons
options.C: The ceiling tiles above the bed
options.D: The upper wall corners of the room

explanation: High-touch surfaces are objects frequently contacted by patient and staff hands, making them primary vectors for cross-contamination. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of allowing a chemical disinfectant to remain wet on a surface for its specified dwell time?

options.A: To ensure sufficient contact time to destroy pathogenic microorganisms
options.B: To create a visible residue that proves the surface was cleaned
options.C: To prevent the cleaning cloth from sticking to the furniture
options.D: To neutralize harsh chemical fumes before staff enter the room

explanation: Disinfectants require a specific duration of continuous contact with pathogens to successfully break down cell walls and inactivate them. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h6)

question: Which category of healthcare waste belongs in a yellow infectious waste bag?

options.A: Soiled dressings and cotton swabs contaminated with body fluids
options.B: Used metallic needles and broken glass ampoules
options.C: Expired pharmaceutical syrups and chemical reagents
options.D: Non-hazardous office paper and food packaging waste

explanation: Yellow bags are universally designated for infectious items contaminated with blood, secretions, and excretions. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h7)

question: Why is point-of-generation waste segregation crucial in clinical wards?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any chemical disinfection of patient rooms
options.B: It prevents infectious materials from being mixed with general waste, reducing exposure risks
options.C: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing heavy-duty cleaning chemicals
options.D: It speeds up the process of making patient beds in the morning

explanation: Sorting waste right where it is generated ensures hazardous items do not accidentally contaminate non-hazardous waste streams. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h7)

question: What is the first immediate action a nurse should take after sustaining a needle-stick injury?

options.A: Squeeze the wound forcefully to express trapped blood
options.B: Wash the puncture site thoroughly with soap and running water
options.C: Apply a tight tourniquet proximal to the wound to trap blood
options.D: Report immediately to the hospital pharmacy for antibiotic drugs

explanation: Washing with soap and water is the immediate first aid step; squeezing or scrubbing can traumatize tissue and increase viral entry. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h8)

question: Why is timely reporting and evaluation critical after an occupational exposure to bloodborne pathogens?

options.A: To ensure the nurse is immediately suspended from clinical duties for weeks
options.B: To fulfill legal paperwork requirements without affecting clinical health
options.C: To determine which colleague was responsible for leaving the sharp exposed
options.D: To determine source risk and initiate post-exposure prophylaxis within the optimal window

explanation: Post-exposure prophylaxis for infections like HIV is most effective when administered as quickly as possible following exposure. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h8)
